en.content:
A senior Chinese official’s visit to Hong Kong to inspect the city’s five-year planning and the Northern Metropolis agenda is more than a routine political courtesy. It reflects a clear expectation that Hong Kong’s future—especially in tech development and space along the Northern Metropolis corridor—must be visibly aligned with the country’s broader development plans. For residents, the practical question is simple: will alignment translate into deliverables that improve everyday opportunities, from jobs and start-up support to housing and connectivity?

The “alignment” theme should, however, be understood as a two-way discipline. For Beijing, the goal is to ensure that Hong Kong’s unique strengths—professional services, finance, logistics, legal and systems expertise—can be harnessed to serve national priorities in a stable, predictable manner. For Hong Kong, the challenge is to preserve institutional confidence and implementation capability while pursuing new momentum. In this sense, the visit can be read as an effort to tighten implementation after years in which public confidence has often been tested by economic uncertainties and cross-border frictions.

Still, the real test will not be the inspection tour; it will be follow-through. If the Northern Metropolis and tech hub are to matter beyond press releases, policy coordination must focus on the things that businesses and young professionals feel first: streamlined licensing and procurement, credible talent pipelines, support for R&D and commercialization, and public infrastructure that reduces time and cost. Just as important is governance clarity—so that stakeholders can plan, invest, and hire without constantly recalibrating to shifting expectations.

Ultimately, Hong Kong’s development path under national integration should be framed as mutual benefit rather than one-directional instruction. The city can contribute to the country’s modernization while asking for space to leverage its strengths and for time-bound benchmarks that demonstrate tangible results. A constructive inspection should therefore be judged by outcomes: measurable progress in infrastructure, innovation capacity, and inclusive economic opportunity that strengthens—rather than crowds out—Hong Kong’s own dynamism.
en.topic_title: Chinese official Xia Baolong to visit Hong Kong, inspect city’s 5-year plan, Northern Metropolis

zh.content:
近排《華盛頓郵報》就本港國安修例嘅論述，再次引爆政界攻防。特區政府同立法機關以「無根據指控」作回應，外部傳媒亦用「國安更新」作框架，兩邊都用自己一套語言講同一個制度，最終社會爭議唔會因為口號而收斂。喺香港，一切涉及國家安全嘅法律議題，本身就容易被政治化、被選擇性解讀：支持者擔心的是威脅嚴重性同執法需要；反對者（或批評者）擔心嘅則係程序透明度、權利保障同「寒蟬效應」。問題係，當外媒批評一出，若只用否定式回應而冇同時提供可核實嘅具體資料、風險評估同救濟路徑，公眾就更難分辨係事實差異、法律理解分歧，定係純粹政治宣傳。

不過，亦要承認：國安條文唔係一般政策辯論咁簡單，因為當局必然會考慮保安需要、情報保護同執法有效性。換言之，外媒可以質疑，但不能以整體敘事取代逐條分析；同樣，政府可以堅稱「無根據」，但更應該用清晰方法交代「依據乜嘢、作出乜嘢、法院／程序點樣處理」：例如修例相對舊有機制究竟新增咗邊種權力、觸發條件係咩、監察由邊個負責、當事人如何申請法律援助或提出司法覆核。喺法治社會，最能夠消減對立嘅，往往唔係更大聲嘅否定，而係可供驗證嘅解釋同制度運作嘅細節。

更深一層睇，今次風波其實反映香港仍然欠缺一個「公共理解」的共同底座：即使不同立場人士都同意國家安全重要，亦未必同意同一套保障公眾權利嘅標準。當外部批評同內部宣示互相打架，社會就容易走向兩極——要嘛全盤接受、要嘛全盤排斥。作為市民，我哋更需要一個能長期運作嘅討論機制：以條文文本為中心、以司法與監察為依歸、以過往案例（在不涉及敏感資訊前提下）作參照，逐步建立信任，而唔係每逢新聞就重演「指控—駁斥」循環。

因此，我嘅立場係：政府應繼續捍衛制度完整同回應外媒不準確之處，但同時要提高公共溝通質素——把「無根據」具體化，把抽象原則落到程序與監察。國安議題愈需要透明，唔係因為要削弱安全，而係因為只有讓公眾理解制度運作，先至可以減少誤讀、降低對立、提升合規與信任。香港唔缺聲音，缺嘅係能夠讓人逐點對照、逐步判斷嘅證據與解釋。

en.topic_title: Hong Kong health authority urges vulnerable groups to get free Covid jabs before gap in supply
en.topic_summary:
Vulnerable Hongkongers are being urged by the Centre for Health Protection (CHP) to get their Covid-19 jabs before current stocks expire.



A baby receiving a Covid-19 vaccine. Photo: GovHK. 



The renewed call comes after the government confirmed two severe paediatric cases of Covid-19 infection, involving a one-year-old boy and a 19-month-old boy. 



The CHP said last week that the two children were in critical condition and neither had received a Covid vaccine.



CHP Controller Dr Edwin T

Build on it by ensuring clear outreach, convenient clinic hours, and transparent expiry info to avoid waste; pair with public education on vaccine safety and the continued importance of non-pharmacological measures for at-risk populations.

messages.name: GLM
messages.content: I strongly agree. Transparent expiry tracking and targeted outreach are vital to maximize uptake before the supply gap. Trusting the CHP’s guidance and streamlining access ensures vulnerable groups, especially children, are protected efficiently without wasting valuable public health resources.

messages.name: DeepSeek
messages.content: Absolutely agree. Prioritizing clear communication and accessible appointments for parents is crucial. The CHP's proactive reminders and free jabs are key to preventing severe cases in unvaccinated children, safeguarding public health efficiently.
